review_notes: I read the whole file and the places that use its lemmas: AllOrderDriftFieldDecomposition.lean, PacketLiftedFlowData.lean, and FieldTowerAlgebra.add_pointField. I also checked the definitions of Budget.fieldTower, pressureTower, pointField and pointPressure. I found no rewrite cycles and no competing simp rules in this file, since it has no simp attributes at all. The only simp-interface issue I found is that the two canonical-representative bridge lemmas are not simp lemmas. The file has no @[simp] anywhere, but the surrounding library uses @[simp] widely. Every use of these lemmas needs an explicitly instantiated term. I did not run Lean, so I did not check how @[simp] would interact with the other lemmas. The suggestion depends on the LHS `FieldTower.pointField` being syntactically reachable, and I think it is, because both sides are applications of `pointField`.

findings.excerpt:
theorem Budget.pressureTower_pointField (t : Icc (0 : ℝ) T) :
    (B.pressureTower P).pointField t = B.pointPressure P t :=
findings.problem: Each lemma is the canonical normalisation of the tower-level `FieldTower.pointField` (the representative that `pointField_unique` picks) to the concrete `Budget.pointField` or `Budget.pointPressure`. The statement is oriented from the abstract tower accessor to the concrete constructed object. It has no hypotheses beyond the arguments and cannot loop, because the RHS no longer mentions `fieldTower` or `pressureTower`. It is still not a simp lemma. Every use has to instantiate it by hand, as in `simpa only [Budget.graphCorrectionWordPath,B.correctionTower_pointField P t]` (lines 62 and 69), the two `rw [... B.correctionTower_pointField P t]` calls in AllOrderDriftFieldDecomposition.lean, and the `simpa only [Q.correctionTower_pointField P s]` calls in PacketLiftedFlowData.lean. Any simp call that meets `(B.fieldTower P).pointField t` therefore leaves the abstract form unchanged, and a user must remember the lemma name and its explicit `P t` arguments.
findings.proposed_change: Mark both lemmas `@[simp]`: `@[simp] theorem Budget.correctionTower_pointField ...` and `@[simp] theorem Budget.pressureTower_pointField ...`. The call sites could then drop the explicit instantiation, for example `simpa [Budget.graphCorrectionWordPath] using ...` or `simp only [Budget.correctionTower_pointField]`. Check that `FieldTower.add_pointField` still composes with them in `correctedFieldTower_pointField`.
findings.benefit: Expressions such as `(B.fieldTower P).pointField t` would normalise automatically to `B.pointField P t`. That gives one canonical pointwise representative for all downstream a.e. statements about the correction and pressure. It removes the manual `P t` instantiation at the four or more call sites and keeps later results from having to restate the bridge.
